title: Subcellular fractionation of zebrafish embryos and mitochondrial calcium uptake application
protocol: Collect embryos at the one-cell stage in a 35 mm Petri dish with E3 medium (at least 100 embryos per condition).
Place the embryos into a pre-chilled dounce glass and add 1 ml of ice-cold MB buffer.
Homogenize for 10 times in ice with a loose-fitting pestle until all embryo’s chorions are removed.
Let the homogenate settle on ice for 10 minutes.
Transfer the homogenate into a pre-chilled 1.5 ml microcentrifuge tube and centrifuge at 300 g for 5 min.
Re-spin the supernatant at 300 g for 5 min to pellet any cells left (optional).
Resuspend pellet containing the cells with 1 ml of cold-MB buffer.
Disrupt the cells with a 1 mL syringe and a 26 G x 2/3 needle 50 times on ice.
Check homogenization by placing 2 μl on a microscope slide and visualizing cell lysis under phase-contrast microscopy.
Centrifuge cell lysate twice at 1,500 g for 10 minutes to eliminate nuclei.
Transfer the supernatant containing mitochondria, cytosol and microsomes into a new pre-chilled 1.5 ml centrifuge tube.
Spin the supernatant twice at 10,600 g for 10 minutes to pellet mitochondria (labeled as mito-I).
Remove and store supernatant on ice (labeled as ER-I) for endoplasmic reticulum membranes isolation.
Gently resuspend the mito-I pellet with 1 ml of cold MB buffer.
Centrifuge again at 10,600 g for 10 minutes.
Discard the supernatant and save the pellet as mitochondria.
Gently resuspend mitochondria in 50 μl of cold MB buffer.
Determine the protein concentration of the sample (Bradford).
Store at -20°C for further investigations (western blot) if not used immediately.
Place the ER-I supernatant (from step 13) into a pre-chilled ultracentrifuge tube and equilibrate the rotor carefully.
Spin at 100,000 g for 1 hour at +4°C.
Carefully discard the supernatant and gently resuspend the pellet containing ER membrane in 50 μl of cold MB buffer.
Determine the amount of microsome proteins (Bradford).
Store at -20°C for further investigations (western blot) if not used immediately.
Wash twice the mitochondrial pellet mito-I (from step 12) with 1 ml of fresh cold KCL medium.
Centrifuge 10 minutes at 10,600 g at +4°C.
Determine the amount of mitochondrial proteins using the Bradford assay.
Transfer 75 μg of proteins into a new 1.5 ml centrifuge tube.
Adjust the volume to 1 ml with KCL medium.
Centrifuge for 10 minutes at 10,600 g at +4°C.
Gently resuspend the pellet with 180 μl of KCL medium containing 1 μM of the cytosolic calcium probe OregonGreen 5N.
Transfer all the volume into a well of a black 96-well plate with flat and transparent bottom.
Measure OregonGreen 5N fluorescence intensity using a Mithras LB 940 multimode microplate reader with excitation at 485 nm and emission at 510 nm.
Measure fluorescence intensity every 2 seconds for 5 minutes.
After 30 seconds, inject 20 μl of KCL buffer supplemented with 200 μM CaCl₂ (final concentration of CaCl₂ 20 μM).
The decrease in fluorescence intensity following the peak induced by CaCl₂ injection is representative of mitochondrial calcium uptake.
